Subjective:
- Current issues: Patient reports new onset right knee pain after stepping off a curb yesterday. Describes dull, aching pain, worsened by walking and climbing stairs. No locking or catching. Mild swelling noticed.
- Past medical history: Hypertension.
- Medications: Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Penicillin (rash).
- Social history: Walks dog daily, no tobacco or alcohol use. Lives independently.

Objective:
- Inspection: Mild swelling noted over right knee, no visible deformities or bruising.
- Palpation: Mild tenderness over medial joint line of right knee.
- Range of motion: Slightly limited due to pain, full extension possible.
- Gait: Antalgic on right.
- No erythema or warmth.
- Vitals: Not documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Right Knee Pain:
   - Assessment: Likely medial meniscal strain or mild sprain/contusion.
   - Differential diagnosis: 
     - Medial meniscus injury (most likely; supported by DDx, consistent with transcript).
     - Knee osteoarthritis (possible; DDx, consistent).
     - Ligamentous injury (less likely; DDx, consistent).
     - Septic arthritis (unlikely; no fever, warmth, or redness; consistent).
   - Investigations:
     - None ordered at this time; will consider imaging if symptoms persist or worsen.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Rest, ice, compression, elevation (RICE) advised.
     - Over-the-counter NSAIDs recommended (specific medication not documented).
     - Follow-up in one week or sooner if worsening symptoms.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected elements: No documentation of full medication list beyond Lisinopril; vital signs not recorded; functional or occupational impairment not discussed.
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: No conflicts noted.
● Brief comment on transcript quality: Transcript clear, complete; no inaudible sections detected.
